{{Quote|Cerea is a beautiful world, but it is&hellip; backward.|Silais|<ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 135" />}}
'''Cerea''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. The [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Cerean/Legends|Cerean]] [[Species/Legends|species]], Cerea was notable for its inhabitants' harmonious relationship with nature. Technology and pollution were frowned upon by the conservative government, a major point in the planet's decision not to join the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. The Cerean population mainly lived in giant buildings that took up a minimum of space, allowing the remainder of the planet's area to be employed as farmland. Foreign immigrants and visitors were, with a few exceptions, only allowed in Cerea's [[Outsider Citadel/Legends|Outsider Citadels]], enormous buildings erected to let non-Cereans practice their technological ways. This ensured that the foreigners' technology did not contaminate Cerea's nature, but also led to a concentration of criminal elements within the Citadels.

Cerea was ruled by the [[Council of Elders (Cerea)|Council of Elders]], which in turn was led by a [[President/Legends|president]]. The planet was for the most part ignored by the Republic until a few years prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Cerea's seclusion caused a unique culture to develop, one that focused on other values than the mainstream galactic civilization. In [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], Cerea was the site of a [[Battle of Cerea|battle]] between the Republic and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], which had an adverse effect on the planet's relatively untouched nature.

==Description==
{{Quote|I see a world and a people in harmony with ''nature'', who ''choose'' not to sully their waters and their air with noxious emissions of motorized craft!|Ki-Adi-Mundi|<ref name="R1" />}}
[[File:Cerea_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A view of Cerea from space]]
Located in the Mid Rim region of the galaxy, Cerea's system was home to no less than three suns. Cerea was situated far away from other planets, which meant it was isolated from the galactic community for several millennia.<ref name="KOTOR Campaign Guide">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> The planet's remote location made it a relatively safe place; an invasion by any of the galaxy's factions was unlikely throughout its history due to the sheer cost of such a long-distance war. However, this also meant that interstellar trade was both laborious and expensive.<ref name="Prelude to Rebellion" />

Cerea was a planet that went relatively untouched by pollution and advanced technology. This was due to the native Cerean species, who worked to preserve Cerean nature, even at the cost of both prosperity and technological advancement.<ref name="Prelude to Rebellion" /> As a result, Cerea was a lush, green world that was covered by vegetation, save for some mountainous regions<ref name="Prelude to Rebellion" /> and several large [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> Cerea's vegetation consisted mostly of grass, bushes, and [[Palm tree/Legends|palm]]-like trees.<ref name="Prelude to Rebellion" /> The planet was home to an abundance of rivers, which were used for transportation.<ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 135" />

[[File:Cereawithcitadel.jpg|thumb|Cerean landscape near an Outsider Citadel]]
Among the few sources of pollution on the planet were the enormous Outsider Citadels, built at the request of the Galactic Republic to house non-Cerean immigrants. Technology was allowed in these structures, which, despite the strict supervision of the Cerean government, were riddled with poverty and various forms of crime. The numerous plains of Cerea were the galaxy's only source of the organic matter [[malium]], which was required in the growth cycle of the native [[tecave]] plant, which in turn produced the euphoria-inducing substance [[Guilea/Legends|guilea]]. The effects of guilea made it a desirable trading commodity, particularly for crime lords such as [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], who sought to synthesize malium to produce his own guilea.<ref name="Prelude to Rebellion" />

==History==
===Early history===
At some point in Cerea's history, the Cerean species, led by [[Bi-Dar Tyunda]], founded a government that encompassed their entire planet.<ref name="Ultimate Alien Anthology" /> Although it is not known whether Tyunda's government originally included it, a Council of Elders came to be the governing body of Cerea.<ref name="Prelude to Rebellion" />

Cerea was introduced to the rest of the galaxy around the time of the [[Mandalorian Wars]], when it was discovered by [[Hyperspace Navigator's Guild]] scouts. Dubbing the planet "36-AFE-2C", these first visitors reported no sightings of intelligent life or useful resources. Shortly after its discovery, the [[Arkanian/Legends|Arkanian]] corporation [[The Adasca BioMechanical Corporation of Arkania|Adascorp]] sent an expedition to Cerea. For reasons unknown, the native Cereans did not welcome these first extraterrestial guests, resulting in the Adascorp agents kidnapping an entire native village and leaving behind several damaged starships. This violent encounter, coupled with the pollution from the discarded Adascorp vessels, caused the Cerean people to adopt an isolationist and anti-technological mindset that would influence their culture for millennia.<ref name="KOTOR Campaign Guide" />

Cerea remained fairly isolated over the next few thousand years; the only contact consisted by and large of Navigators' Guild survey ships passing by.<ref name="KOTOR Campaign Guide" /> Despite this, the Cerean known as [[Paran Am-Ris]] engaged with the politics of the Republic, eventually becoming a [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] and later the interim [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] following the murder of [[Berooken|Supreme Chancellor Berooken]] during the [[Sacking of Coruscant]]. A few years prior to [[67 BBY/Legends|67 BBY]] that Cereans fully established contact with the Galactic Republic and the galaxy at large. Finding certain aspects of Republic politics disturbing, Cerea's government decided not to join the trans-galactic union.<ref name="Vow of Justice" /><ref name="Roleplaying Game Revised Core Rulebook">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Revised Core Rulebook]]''</ref><ref name="Prelude to Rebellion" /> At least one rural community on Cerea was lorded over by bandits in the years leading up to the Clone Wars, but the Cerean [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Ki-Adi-Mundi/Legends|Ki-Adi-Mundi]] ended their reign in 67 BBY.<ref name="Vow of Justice" />

===Pro-technology movement===
{{Quote|The galaxy is laughing. Listen! Hear the laughter ringing out from the ''stars''! It's ''you'' who are the joke!|Bron, at a political rally|<ref name="R1" />}}
[[File:Protechrally.jpg|thumb|left|140px|Bron, speaking at a political rally]]
In [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], the Galactic Republic dispatched several diplomats to convince Cerea to join their galactic government. The Republic was interested in modernizing the planet, particularly the way Cereans handled their plentiful natural resources. Some diplomats, such as [[Silais]], unsuccessfully attempted to convince the Cerean Council of Elders. Others, such as the charismatic [[Bron (Human)|Bron]], sought to appeal to Cerea's younger generations. Through huge political rallies, he gathered a large amount of supporters with fiery speeches that condemned Cerea's "antique" traditions as the laughing stock of the galaxy. Bron was not above employing illegal means to raise support for his pro-tech movement; his campaign was in part financed by the gangster Jabba Desilijic Tiure, who traded technology such as [[Swoop/Legends|swoops]] for malium. Bron was also aligned with [[Dorr-Femi-Bonmi]], a member of the Council of Elders who acted as the pro-tech movement's spy in the government's affairs, while profiting from their trading operations. After Ki-Adi-Mundi and his daughter, [[Sylvn (Cerean)|Sylvn]], exposed the connection to Jabba, Bron and his movement died down, though Elder [[Nar-Somo-Dali]] suspected the lack of activity was only temporary.<ref name="Prelude to Rebellion" />

===Clone Wars===
At the height of the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], Cerea joined the [[Refugee Relief Movement/Legends|Refugee Resettlement Coalition]], a program run by the Refugee Relief Movement. In doing so, Cerea's government volunteered to allow vast amounts of displaced refugees to settle on the planet. However, the refugees were forbidden from bringing any vehicles or heavy machinery, in accordance with Cerean law.<ref name="HNN 52" />

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] secretly encouraged a tendency in the younger Cerean generation to seek out more technological ways of life. This culminated in the Separatist-aligned [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] holding a number of young Cereans hostage, until Jedi intervention rescued the youths. The planet chose neutrality during the war, which caused both the Republic and the Confederacy to fear the planet would join the other faction's side. This led to the [[Battle of Cerea]] in [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]],<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> which resulted in an estimated 1,000,000 civilian casualties,<ref name="LFC">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/livingforce/swlf20041223|text=Disapproval|int=Disapproval}}</ref> the despoiling of much of the planet's pristine nature,<ref name="Seirr Tarr DB">{{DB|character|tarrseirr|Seirr, Tarr}}</ref> as well as the assassination of the reigning planetary president, [[Bo-Ro-Tara]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

===Isolationism===
Following the Clone Wars, the Cerean government adopted an isolationist stance, choosing not to get involved in galactic politics. As a result, the planet remained secluded during the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]],<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /><ref name="Roleplaying Game Revised Core Rulebook" /> although at least a few Cereans found themselves working for the Imperial military.<ref name="Death Star">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']]</ref> The Empire appointed Imperial Governor [[Andreo Tagge]], who brought expertise in agriworld management. While the Cerean Council of Elders was officially allowed to continue governing the planet, Governor Tagge progressively annexed and industrialized increasing portions of Cerea’s arable land each year, in blatant violation of the planet’s terms of surrender.<ref name=":0">[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Force and Destiny'' Core Rulebook]]</ref>

Meanwhile, a growing offworlder presence introduced small technological items—such as datapads, glow rods, and other trinkets—into Cerean society, particularly among the youth. These items became points of contention, sparking cultural tensions between the Imperials and the Council of Elders and creating generational rifts within many Cerean families. Although the council filed numerous formal complaints and launched investigations into Imperial overreach, these efforts had little effect, fueling rising discontent with Imperial rule.<ref name=":0" />

Although it is unknown if Cerea eventually joined the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], a Cerean dignitary witnessed the signing of the [[Pellaeon–Gavrisom Treaty]] between the Republic and the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] in [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]].<ref name="EC">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref> Cerea maintained its isolationism even after the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

[[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]] also had little interest in the planet and left it under only a light Imperial supervision. This allowed members of the [[Galactic Alliance Remnant]], [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] in exile and other dissidents to visit Cerea without risking being caught by the [[One Sith|Sith]]. The Cereans, however, continued to view the outsiders as trouble and were even known to hand those seeking refuge over to the Empire in order to avoid a larger Imperial presence on their world.<ref name="LECG">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|A person always takes his home with him, wherever he goes. Worlds are vast&mdash;yet they fit easily into one's heart.|Ki-Adi Mundi|<ref name="ETM">''[[Star Wars: Emissaries to Malastare]]''</ref>}}
[[File:KiAdiMundi.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Ki-Adi-Mundi, a Cerean Jedi Master]]
The planet's dominant species were the native [[Cerean/Legends|Cereans]], a peaceful people with large, cone-shaped craniums. The Cereans were not very technologically advanced, instead preferring to rely on non-polluting tools and vehicles, as part of their philosophy that called for a harmonious relationship with nature.<ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 135" /> The species generally preferred to stay on Cerea, although the few individuals who left for the galaxy on occasion rose to prominent positions<ref name="Saga Edition Core Rulebook" /> such as [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]]<ref name="Prelude to Rebellion" /> or [[Doctor/Legends|neurosurgeon]].<ref name="Death Star" />The Cereans suffered from a low male-to-female birth ratio; females outnumbered the males twenty to one, which led to a culture of [[polygamy]].<ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 135" /> By [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] the Cerean population numbered 450 million.<ref name="HNN 52" />

Non-sentient species on Cerea included the [[Aryx/Legends|aryx]], an avian species that possessed great stamina and speed, that was domesticated by the Cereans for transportation.<ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 135" /> The rivers of Cerea were home to the [[crown of silk]] creature, a short-lived species that found nourishment in the brain energies of its victims.<ref name="Ultimate Adversaries" />

==Locations==
===Tecave City===
{{Main|Tecave City}}
[[File:Tecave_City.jpg|thumb|left|Tecave City]]
Most of Cerea's inhabitants resided in large cities, allowing for much of the planet's area to be employed for farming purposes. This trend also applied to Tecave City, the planet's largest city and capital.<ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 135" /> Notable for its ornamented, architecturally distinctive buildings, Tecave City shared its name with the tecave plant. The one deviation from the semi-tall buildings that characterized the city was the structure that housed the Council of Elders&mdash;a massive, metallic edifice seemingly overgrown with vegetation.<ref name="Prelude to Rebellion" />

===Outsider Citadels===
{{Main|Outsider Citadel/Legends}}
As part of an agreement with the Galactic Republic, several Outsider Citadels were built to house non-Cerean immigrants and visitors. The Citadels were enormous buildings that each housed an entire city, and were among the few locations where non-Cerean technology was allowed.<ref name="Prelude to Rebellion" /> The concentration of polluting technology and the relative lack of space caused some Citadels to devolve into environmentally contaminating and overpopulated ghettos.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> Crime was rampant, despite the supervision of Cerean police forces.<ref name="Prelude to Rebellion" />

==Behind the scenes==
Writer [[Jan Strnad]] created Cerea for the [[Star Wars: Prelude to Rebellion|''Prelude to Rebellion'' arc]] of the ''[[Star Wars: Republic]]'' series of comics. When naming the planet, Strnad sent in a number of suggestions to [[Dark Horse Comics]] and [[Lucasfilm]], among them "France." They chose the name Cerea, which Strnad had come up with based on the Roman goddess of harvest, [[Wikipedia:Ceres (mythology)|Ceres]]. Strnad felt the name fit with the agricultural nature of Cerea.<ref name="cswu">{{WebCite|url=http://www.cswu.cz/woc/int/jan_strnad_en.html|text=Interview with Jan S. Strnad|archivedate=20010217004748}}</ref>
